title: Rubio says Ukraine hit ships tied to U.S. oil interests
excerpt: Rubio repeated the claim in an Oct. 19 New York Post report, but the supplied reporting does not identify the ships or show whether they were U.S.-owned, U.S.-flagged or linked by cargo.
body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday in Uzbekistan that Ukraine had struck ships carrying American-owned oil in the Black Sea, according to the New York Post. In the same report, Rubio also repeated that the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing used to warn Kyiv about Russian ballistic missile attacks.

“There’s been no pause. Zelensky should be focused on bringing an end to this war,” Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan, the Post reported. He also said, “We have seen strikes on energy vessels in the Black Sea. And there’s been complaints, a lot, because we have American companies calling us and saying, ‘Hey, that was our oil on that ship that was hit by Ukraine.’”

The report said Rubio added that he did not believe Ukraine intentionally targeted the vessels. It did not identify which ships he meant, or say whether they were American-owned, U.S.-flagged or merely carrying cargo tied to U.S. interests.

Rubio made a similar accusation in a Sept. 22 Fox News interview, according to ABC News. He said then that “American-linked ships, American oil supplies have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine,” while ABC said it was not immediately clear what incidents he was describing.

Kyiv Post reported that Rubio did not publicly name the vessels or clarify whether they were American-owned, U.S.-flagged or connected to the United States through cargo, chartering or energy infrastructure. The outlet said the claim appeared to refer to vessels using Russia’s Black Sea ports to transport oil connected to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which carries Kazakh crude.

ABC News reported that the Caspian Pipeline Consortium counts Chevron and ExxonMobil among its top shareholders. Rubio also told Fox News that the United States supported the idea of an energy infrastructure ceasefire in which neither side would target the other’s energy supplies.

The exact ships or cargoes Rubio was referring to remain unidentified in the supplied reporting. What is clear from the available accounts is that he has continued to press the argument that Ukraine should avoid strikes affecting energy shipping and supplies with American links, while Washington and Kyiv dispute how U.S. intelligence and wartime targeting are being handled.
